issues.description: Interface naming mismatch: the problem statement and template expect an interface named 'Milkable' with method messageOnMilk(), but the solution introduces an interface named 'Dairy' (with the correct method) and leaves Milkable.java empty. Several concrete classes (Seal, Goat) in the solution implement 'Dairy' instead of 'Milkable'. This discrepancy is structural and will confuse students about which interface to create and implement, and will break compilation/tests that reference Milkable.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the interface name consistent across all artifacts. Rename the solution's 'Dairy' interface to 'Milkable' (or update the problem/template to refer to 'Dairy'), delete or populate the empty Milkable.java accordingly, and update all classes (Seal, Goat, etc.) to implement the correctly named interface so that the template, specification, and solution align.

issues.description: The problem statement and template reference an interface named 'Milkable' (with method messageOnMilk()), but the solution implements this concept under the different identifier 'Dairy' (Dairy.java) while leaving Milkable.java empty. This naming divergence (Milkable vs Dairy) refers to the same conceptual entity (the milk-providing interface) and will confuse students mapping the requirement to the code: they will expect to implement/use Milkable, but the solution uses Dairy, and the empty Milkable.java further obscures the intended mapping.
issues.suggestedFix: Unify the identifier for the milkable interface across all artifacts. Rename Dairy.java to Milkable.java (or vice-versa in problem/template) and ensure the interface declares messageOnMilk(). Update Seal and Goat to implement Milkable and remove or populate the empty Milkable.java so that the problem statement, template, and solution use the same interface name 'Milkable'.
